opening_message:
Ticket 1: Morgan Swanson (employee ID E037) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E037.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Morgan Swanson (E037), full-time Engineer, requests write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write; role does not own Payroll so admin is not available. Recommended: write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Morgan Swanson (E037) as a contractor with basic security training (note in memory said full-time, but security record is authoritative). Contractors max at read without advanced training; requested write is above max, so grant read.
reason: Morgan Swanson (E037) requested write access to Payroll. Security agent's record (authoritative) shows Morgan is a contractor with basic security training, so the maximum allowed level is read (contractors may have read, or write only with advanced security training; admin is never allowed). Since the requested write exceeds the maximum, the maximum (read) is granted.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee: Morgan Swanson (E037), requests write access to Payroll.

Two notes:
- HR note: role Engineer, employment type full_time, recommendation write.
- Security note: role Engineer, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read. Security says security record is authoritative, contractor max read without advanced training.

Access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist role. Morgan is Engineer, so doesn't own Payroll.

Discrepancy: HR says full-time, Security says contractor with basic training.

As the approver, I need to consider the conflicting info. The Security agent says their record is authoritative. The policy differs: if full-time, max is write; requested write is at or below max, so grant write. If contractor with basic training, max is read; requested write above max, grant read.

Which source to trust? The team memory shows both notes were written on ticket 1, same ticket. The security note explicitly says "note in memory said full-time, but security record is authoritative."

Hmm, as the Approver, I need to make final decision. The security agent asserts their record is authoritative. Typically, security records would be authoritative for employment type. So contractor with basic training: max read. Requested write is above max, so grant read.

Let me submit decision: read.

Evidence: Morgan is a contractor with basic security training (security record authoritative). Contractors max at read without advanced training. Payroll is not owned by Engineer role. Requested write is above max, so grant max read.
